o: Recall the essential ideas of characters and images.
c: Character sets map symbols to numerical codes stored in binary; ASCII and Unicode are examples.
A bitmap stores the colour of each pixel in a grid. Resolution is width in pixels × height in pixels.
Colour depth is the number of bits per pixel. More bits allow more possible colours.
Uncompressed size (bits) = width × height × colour depth; divide by eight for bytes (ignoring metadata).

Explain one difference between ASCII and Unicode. [3]

k.q: Predict the uncompressed bitmap size in bytes.
k.code:
width = 20
height = 10
bitsPerPixel = 8
bytes = width * height * bitsPerPixel DIV 8
print(bytes)
p: Extend to calculate size when bitsPerPixel = 16.
k.a: 20×10×8÷8 = 200 bytes; doubled height -> 400 bytes; 16 bits per pixel -> 400 bytes with original dimensions.
